harvest_bucket: Structural heart disease, cardiomyopathy, and ischemia
outcomes_summary: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) is a common condition with a prevalence of 15%-20% in general population. Prior studies have suggested that deep learning model (DLM)-enabled electrocardiogram (ECG) systems can aid LVH detection and cardiovascular risk assessment; however, conventional manual ECG criteria have limited sensitivity and their prognostic utility remains suboptimal.

title: EAGLE Trial: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiogram for Low Ejection Fraction
outcomes_summary: Pragmatic cluster RCT of AI-ECG for low EF in 22641 primary-care visits across 45 sites; intervention increased new low-EF diagnoses (2.1% vs 1.6%; OR 1.32).

title: Detection of Hypokalemia, Hyponatremia, and Hyperkalemia in Heart Failure Patients Using Artificial Intelligence Techniques via Electrocardiography
outcomes_summary: The accuracy rates of the DLM in detecting hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and hyperkalemia were 83.33%, 95.33%, and 95.77%, respectively.
condition: left ventricular systolic dysfunction / low EF

title: An Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiogram to Evaluate Patients With Dyspnea in the Emergency Department
harvest_bucket: LV systolic dysfunction and heart failure
outcomes_summary: Of the 2412 patients, 966 (40%) were found to have cardiac dyspnea, and the remaining 1446 (60%) were noncardiac. The AI-ECG-estimated diastolic function was divided into 4 groups: 922 (38.2%) were normal, 245 (10.2%) grade 1, 1192 (49.4%) grade 2, and 53 (2.2%) grade 3.

title: Screening and diagnosis of cardiovascular disease using artificial intelligence-enabled cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.
source_type: Large retrospective development and external validation study
outcomes_summary: Two-stage cine plus LGE system achieved AUC 0.988 for screening and 0.991 for diagnosis, with strong internal and external performance and cardiologist-level or better results for some tasks.
validation_status: Internal and external validation; proof-of-concept for scalable computerized CMR interpretation
task: Automated CMR screening and diagnosis across multiple diseases

title: A novel deep learning system for STEMI prognostic prediction from multi-sequence cardiac magnetic resonance.
outcomes_summary: DeepSTEMI used 610 registry patients for development and 334 external-validation patients, reaching AUC 0.894 and identifying a 20-fold risk difference between predicted high- and low-risk groups.
validation_status: External validation across three independent cardiac centers
task: Post-STEMI 2-year MACE prediction from multisequence CMR

title: A deep learning model could screen for coronary heart disease from a "pseudo-normal" electrocardiogram
harvest_bucket: Structural heart disease, cardiomyopathy, and ischemia
outcomes_summary: The model was developed using a dataset comprising 21,240 ECGs from 15,995 patients at SAH, with 4248 ECGs serving as the internal testing set. Additionally, 2572 ECGs from FAH were utilized as the external testing set.

title: Artificial intelligence in electrocardiogram-based prediction of heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis
outcomes_summary: Meta-analysis of ECG-based AI for heart-failure prediction found pooled performance around 0.76 with high heterogeneity, suggesting promise but limited transportability and clinical-validity evidence.

title: Semi-supervised segmentation of cardiac chambers from LGE-CMR using feature consistency awareness.
outcomes_summary: Semi-supervised segmentation achieved Dice around 88-91% on atrial and 87-89% on ventricular tasks using only 10-20% labeled data.
validation_status: Technical validation; dataset-level rather than prospective clinical validation
task: LGE chamber segmentation with limited labels

title: Challenges in clinical translation of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging radiomics in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy: a narrative review.
outcomes_summary: Details practical workflow and translational bottlenecks for MRI radiomics in HCM, DCM, and myocarditis.
task: Radiomics translation in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy
